issues.passage: After the last factory closed, the brand became ubiquitous on store shelves nationwide.
issues.why: "Became ubiquitous on store shelves nationwide" is valid, natural use of ubiquitous = present/found everywhere. The factory-closure clause is only pragmatically odd; it does not make the word itself a misuse. A student who knows the definition would rightly accept this passage.

fix.correctPassage: Smartphones are now so ubiquitous that many public spaces assume constant connectivity.
wrongPassages: The orchid is ubiquitous in the region—only a single wild specimen has ever been documented.
She kept her ubiquitous notes in one locked drawer that no colleague was allowed to open.
After the last factory closed, the brand became ubiquitous—vanishing from shelves within weeks and never restocked.
